slot.brief: Given rate constant of a zero-order reaction, find concentration remaining after a stated time (or time to reach zero).

stem: A zero-order reaction has $[\text{A}]_0 = 0.48\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ and $k = 8.0\times10^{-4}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$. How long will it take for $\text{A}$ to be completely consumed?

verdicts.working: For a zero-order reaction, t = [A]0/k = 0.48/(8.0×10^-4) = 600 s.

working:
$[\text{A}]_t=[\text{A}]_0-kt$; at complete consumption, $[\text{A}]_t=0$.\
$t=\dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{k}=\dfrac{0.48}{8.0\times10^{-4}}=600\ \text{s}$.

Independent check: For a zero-order reaction, t = [A]0/k = 0.48/(8.0×10^-4) = 600 s.
